uncited: **Define Node Types:** Determine the type of each node based on the split direction of its father.
If a node is split along the x-axis, its children are typed `left` and `right`.
**Identify Common Points:** Identify vertices shared between adjacent blocks.
Due to numerical inaccuracies in vertex extraction, coordinate comparison is unreliable.
Instead, use the property of the Marching Cubes algorithm: a cell edge can generate at most one point.
**Check Restricted Adjacency:** Determine if a completed block $p_1$ can merge with another block $p_2$ (brother) or $n$ (nephew, i.e., a child of $p_1$'s brother).
This criterion ensures that the blocks share a true geometric boundary.
**Simplify Pasted Area:** After merging the meshes, simplify the "pasted area" (the interface) using the same error criteria $E_0$ used during extraction.
*   **Ancestry Check:** When merging a nephew, it is critical to check *all* ancestors of the nephew up to the brother node.
*   **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
Restricted Adjacency Merging was introduced in the context of parallel isosurface extraction for very large geophysical datasets.
